goal.en: Share a different idea without making anyone lose face.
goal.zh: 提出不同意見，又不讓任何人難堪。

background: glass-walled meeting room with a round wooden table, several pendant lamp samples hanging low, a few loose amber bulbs, closed notebooks and pens, a potted fern, soft afternoon light

intro.en: The team is planning the lighting for Harbor Café's new shop. Daniel has just shown his idea.
intro.zh: 團隊正在規劃 Harbor Café 新分店的燈光。丹尼爾剛提出他的構想。

intro.en: Dim amber light everywhere. Think candlelit bar. Cozy, warm, very stylish.
intro.zh: 全場都用昏暗的琥珀色燈光，想像一下燭光酒吧的感覺。溫馨、溫暖，又很有型。

intro.en: But you visited their first shop last week, and half the customers were working on laptops.
intro.zh: 可是你上週去過他們的第一家店，有一半的客人都在用筆電工作。

lines.en: Kai, you visited their first shop. What are your thoughts?
lines.zh: 凱，你去過他們的第一家店。你怎麼看？

choices.en: I like the cozy feeling, but I noticed a lot of customers work on laptops there.
choices.zh: 我喜歡這種溫馨的感覺，但我注意到那裡很多客人會用筆電工作。
choices.tip: 先肯定對方的優點，再用 but I noticed... 帶出你看到的事實，就不會像在否定對方。

choices.en: Honestly, I think it's a really bad idea. Nobody can work in a dark café like that.
choices.zh: 老實說，我覺得這是個很爛的主意。在那麼暗的咖啡廳裡沒人能工作。

lines.en: A bad idea. Okay. Good to know.

story.en: Nobody speaks for ten long seconds. Daniel stops making eye contact with you for the rest of the week.
story.zh: 整整十秒沒人說話。接下來一整週，丹尼爾都不太跟你對上眼。

fail.why: it's a bad idea 太直接，聽起來在否定對方這個人。先肯定再補充：I like..., but I noticed...。

choices.en: Daniel is the senior designer, so I think his idea must be right. I agree.
choices.zh: 丹尼爾是資深設計師，所以我覺得他的想法一定是對的。我同意。

lines.en: Hmm. But I asked what you saw at the shop, Kai.
lines.zh: 嗯……可是我問的是你在店裡看到了什麼，凱。

story.en: The café opens with candlelit lighting. A month later, the client complains that nobody stays to work anymore.
story.zh: 咖啡廳用燭光燈光開幕了。一個月後，客戶抱怨再也沒有人留下來工作了。

fail.why: 在很多英語系職場，主管問你的看法，是真的想聽，不是要你附和資深同事。有不同意見就說：I like..., but I noticed...。

lines.en: Sure, but people go to cafés for the atmosphere, not just to work.
lines.zh: 是沒錯，但大家去咖啡廳是為了氣氛，不只是為了工作。

choices.en: I see your point, but on my visit, most tables had someone studying or working.
choices.zh: 我懂你的意思，但我去的那天，大部分的桌子都有人在讀書或工作。
choices.tip: I see your point, but... 先承認對方的觀點有道理，再用自己看到的事實補充。

choices.en: I am agree with you, but most of people there is working, not for the atmosphere.
choices.zh: 我同意你，但那邊大部分的人是在工作，不是為了氣氛。

lines.en: Wait, so you agree with me? Great, then we'll go with amber.
lines.zh: 等等，所以你同意我？太好了，那就用琥珀色燈光。

story.en: Daniel only hears the first three words. Your point gets lost, and the meeting moves on without it.
story.zh: 丹尼爾只聽到前三個字。你的重點不見了，會議就這樣繼續往下走。

fail.why: agree 是動詞，不加 am：I agree.；「大部分的人」是 most people 或 most of the people，動詞用 are。想表示不同意，用 I see your point, but...。

choices.en: Atmosphere is nice, but the reality is very cruel. People there need to work.
choices.zh: 氣氛是很好，但現實是很殘酷的。那邊的人需要工作。

lines.en: Cruel? Wow. It's... just a café, Kai.
lines.zh: 殘酷？哇。這只是……一家咖啡廳而已，凱。

story.en: The room laughs, but not with you. For the rest of the meeting, Priya calls the project "the cruel café."
story.zh: 大家都笑了，但不是跟著你笑。接下來的會議，普莉雅一直把這個案子叫做「殘酷咖啡廳」。

fail.why: 「現實很殘酷」直譯成 the reality is very cruel，在英文裡太戲劇化。說 I see your point, but on my visit... 用事實說話就好。

lines.en: Dim lighting does look amazing in photos, though. That's free marketing for them.
lines.zh: 不過昏暗的燈光拍照真的很好看耶。這對他們來說是免費的行銷。

choices.en: That's true. Have we considered warm light on the walls and brighter lamps over the tables?
choices.zh: 沒錯。我們有沒有考慮過牆面用暖光，桌子上方用亮一點的燈？
choices.tip: Have we considered...? 用問句提出替代方案，用 we 讓大家一起想，不會像在糾正別人。

choices.en: Speaking of photos, we should take a team photo for Instagram today! The lighting in here is great.
choices.zh: 說到照片，我們今天應該拍張團體照放 Instagram！這裡的光線超好。

lines.en: Maybe later, Kai. Let's get back to the café plan.
lines.zh: 晚點再說吧，凱。我們先回到咖啡廳的企劃。

story.en: The meeting gets back on track, but without your idea. You did get a nice team photo, though.
story.zh: 會議回到正軌，但你的點子沒被提出來。不過你倒是拍到一張很好看的團體照。

fail.why: 大家正在討論燈光方案時突然換話題，會讓你的意見錯過時機。先回應對方，再提出方案：That's true. Have we considered...?。

choices.en: Photos are not important. It's a café, not a studio. People come to drink coffee.
choices.zh: 照片不重要。這是咖啡廳，不是攝影棚。大家是來喝咖啡的。

lines.en: Not important? Photos are half of my job, Kai.
lines.zh: 不重要？照片可是我一半的工作耶，凱。

story.en: Priya was on your side a minute ago. Now she's backing Daniel's amber plan, with great enthusiasm.
story.zh: 一分鐘前普莉雅還站在你這邊。現在她熱烈支持丹尼爾的琥珀色方案。

fail.why: 說別人在意的事 not important，等於否定對方的工作。先說 That's true.，再用 Have we considered...? 把對方的需求也放進方案裡。

lines.en: Two kinds of lighting? Hmm. Wouldn't that cost a lot more?
lines.zh: 兩種燈光？嗯……那不是會貴很多嗎？

choices.en: Possibly, but our Halo lamps are fairly cheap. I could check the numbers if that helps.
choices.zh: 有可能，但我們的 Halo 燈滿便宜的。如果有幫助的話，我可以算一下數字。
choices.tip: possibly、fairly、I could 這類詞讓語氣變軟，再主動提出可以做的事，討論就能往前走。

choices.en: Maybe will cost more, but is not so expensive, I think. I can to check the price for you.
choices.zh: 可能會比較貴，但我覺得沒有那麼貴。我可以幫你查一下價格。

lines.en: So... it costs more, but it isn't expensive? I'm lost.
lines.zh: 所以……會比較貴，但又不貴？我聽不懂了。

story.en: Nobody is sure what you meant. Ms. Wong asks you to "send something in writing," which is never a good sign.
story.zh: 沒人確定你的意思。王經理請你「寫成書面寄給她」，這通常不是好兆頭。

fail.why: 句子要有主詞：It might cost more, but it's not that expensive.；can 後面直接接原形動詞，不加 to：I can check。

choices.en: Sorry, you're right. Maybe it's a stupid idea. Just forget I said anything.
choices.zh: 抱歉，你說得對。也許這是個蠢主意。就當我什麼都沒說。

lines.en: Wait, I actually liked that idea. Why give up so fast?
lines.zh: 等等，我其實滿喜歡那個點子的。怎麼這麼快就放棄？

story.en: Your idea was good, but you dropped it at the first question. The team goes with full amber lighting.
story.zh: 你的點子很好，但第一個問題就讓你棄守。團隊最後決定全部用琥珀色燈光。

fail.why: 被提問不代表被否定，對方只是想多了解。不必馬上道歉撤回，用 Possibly, but... I could check... 繼續把想法說清楚。

lines.en: I like where this is going. Kai, could you work on this with Daniel?
lines.zh: 我喜歡這個方向。凱，你可以跟丹尼爾一起處理這件事嗎？

choices.en: Of course. Daniel, would you be free tomorrow to go over it together?
choices.zh: 當然。丹尼爾，你明天有空一起討論一下嗎？
choices.tip: 討論結束後主動約對方，展現你是想合作，不是想贏。

choices.en: Of course. See, Daniel? I told you my idea was better. Let's do it my way.
choices.zh: 當然。你看吧，丹尼爾？我就說我的點子比較好。就照我的方式做吧。

lines.en: "Your way." Sure. Let me know how that goes.
lines.zh: 「你的方式」。好啊，做得怎麼樣再跟我說。

story.en: You win the meeting but lose your partner. Daniel answers your emails with one word for a week.
story.zh: 你贏了這場會議，卻失去了合作夥伴。整整一週，丹尼爾回你的信都只有一個字。

fail.why: 意見被採納後還強調「我贏了」，會讓對方很沒面子。說 Of course. Daniel, would you be free to go over it together? 把功勞變成合作。

choices.en: Of course. I will cooperate with Daniel very happily and do my best.
choices.zh: 當然。我會很開心地配合丹尼爾，盡我最大的努力。

lines.en: Cooperate? You make it sound like I'm a police officer.
lines.zh: 配合？你講得好像我是警察一樣。

story.en: Everyone laughs. Daniel starts calling your meetings "interviews," and the joke lasts all month.
story.zh: 大家都笑了。丹尼爾開始把你們的會議叫做「偵訊」，這個梗用了一整個月。

fail.why: 「配合」直譯成 cooperate 聽起來很正式，常用在配合調查、配合警方。同事之間說 work with 或 go over it together 就好。

lines.en: Tomorrow at ten works. And Kai, good catch on the laptop crowd.
lines.zh: 明天十點可以。還有凱，筆電族那點你觀察得很好。

story.en: You disagreed, kept your facts clear, and nobody lost face. The final plan has warm walls, bright tables and two happy designers.
story.zh: 你提出了不同意見，用事實說話，也沒讓任何人難堪。最後的方案有溫暖的牆面、明亮的桌面，還有兩位開心的設計師。

notes.explain: 先承認對方說得有道理，再提出不同看法。比直接說 I disagree 柔和很多，類似的還有 That's a good point, but...。

example.en: I see your point, but I'm worried about the budget.
example.zh: 我懂你的意思，但我擔心預算。

notes.explain: 用問句提出替代方案，用 we 讓大家一起想，聽起來像在討論，不像在糾正。後面接名詞或動名詞。

example.en: Have we considered using a different supplier?
example.zh: 我們有沒有考慮過換一家供應商？

notes.zh: 緩衝語：可能／還算／我可以
notes.explain: possibly 讓肯定變得保留，fairly 讓程度變溫和，I could 讓提議變客氣。這些緩衝語能讓不同意見聽起來不刺耳。

example.en: It's fairly simple. I could show you after lunch.
example.zh: 這還算簡單。午餐後我可以示範給你看。

notes.explain: agree 本身就是動詞，前面不加 am。正確說法是 I agree. 或 I don't agree.，要表達部分同意可以說 I partly agree.。

example.en: I agree with you on the colors.

notes.explain: 在很多英語系職場，主管問你的想法，就是真心想聽，即使你是新人。只要語氣委婉、用事實說話，提出不同意見反而會被看作有貢獻。

example.en: That's a fair point. Can I share a different view?
example.zh: 這個觀點很合理。我可以分享一個不同的看法嗎？
